provenance.mode_tail_ownership: Deck/menu, Continue and Event callback groups each reproduce their native code, name, initialized-data and BSS runs in all three original ROMs. The shared event ID is unsigned as established by the original message-handler switch branches.

provenance.map_initialized_owner: The sixty-six original map configuration, callback, task, mode, debug-glyph and floor-name objects form one native 1556-byte initialized-data run in map.c across all regions. Definitions retain original types, bounds, initializer values and regional guards except that the three fourteen-byte level-offset/event arrays use mutable byte storage. Their old const declarations came from decompilation (89d03418 for level offsets and 474e8dcb for event bytes); recovery commit 47811f02 introduced the definitions and custom readonly sections. Mutable spelling is a reconstruction of the native initialized-data organization, not evidence of observed writes. The two floor-name indexes are read by the floor-task helper named by the final task descriptor; the underscore belongs to the map-debug initializer and remains present but unused by the EU renderer. These three objects move from the artificial map_text_data.c storage split into those consumers, with EU localized records retained under shared canonical declarations. Callback descriptors, table references, native compiler offsets and complete regional object/content contracts corroborate the organization. Lower-ROM names and localized text records retain their placements, and this does not assert a complete original source boundary with map_runtime.c or resolve all remaining readonly sections.
provenance.allmap_readonly_geometry: The original 32-byte coordinate span is reconstructed as two const signed-halfword tables of four x/y pairs. func_080D484C indexes the first four-pair rectangle while drawing the four door overlays. The next four pairs form a complete centered 32-pixel square in every original ROM, followed by this same owner's four-direction offset and direction-selection tables. Assigning this dormant but geometrically complete table to the same owner is an explicit source-organization inference; no live use or uniquely recovered original array boundary is claimed. Original ROM scans find no direct pointer to any byte of the second table. Ordinary definitions place the four earlier names, both coordinate tables and the existing readonly suffix in one 218-byte section. All original bytes, existing object extents, code, relocations and RAM are unchanged, and the former absolute coordinate alias and raw data fragment are removed.
